role: 2027 Spring Internship: Vehicle Software Integration Engineer
jd:
Company Information

PACCAR is a global technology leader in the design, manufacture and customer support of high-quality light-, medium- and heavy-duty trucks under the Kenworth, Peterbilt and DAF nameplates. PACCAR also designs and manufactures advanced power trains, provides financial services and information technology, and distributes truck parts related to its principal business.

Requisition Summary

PACCAR Innovation Center has an internship for students currently enrolled in college. This opening is for a Vehicle Software Integration Engineer Intern to add to our Innovation team in Silicon Valley, California.

This is an on-site internship, expected to start in January 2027 and continue through May 2027, with the possibility of extending beyond May based on availability.

Job Responsibilities

You will join PACCAR's Silicon Valley Innovation team, which explores emerging, state-of-the-art vehicle technologies to keep our trucks at the forefront of innovation.

This is a hands-on role. You will build real systems and show the results in a working Class 8 semi-truck. You will work on a next-generation connected vehicle platform made up of three systems: a digital cockpit, a vehicle gateway and a telematics unit. Your job is to take this platform from the lab bench and integrate it into a truck. The work includes, but is not limited to:



-  Studying the truck's electrical, electronic and software systems and overall vehicle architecture to understand how the new platform must fit into it.
-  Identifying the hardware and software changes needed for integration, then putting them in place.
-  Installing the platform in the truck, bringing it up, and validating it.
-  Debugging issues across hardware, software, and vehicle networks.
-  Identifying technical risks early and proposing smart ways to mitigate them early in the program.
-  Coming up with creative solutions when standard approaches don't work.
-  Documenting your work and demonstrating the results to engineers and leadership.

This role suits someone with strong problem-solving skills who enjoys hands-on engineering. If you love challenges, this is for you.

Required Qualifications

The candidate we seek will be currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Mechatronics, Automotive Engineering, or a related program, and will have:



-  Strong understanding of vehicle systems and how they work together
-  Strong understanding of vehicle networking protocols, such as CAN, automotive Ethernet and service-oriented communication (SOME/IP, DDS) or similar
-  Programming and debugging in C/C++, Java or Kotlin; scripting in Python or shell
-  Comfort with Linux: command line, Git, building and cross-compiling software
-  Foundational understanding of vehicle electrical power and grounding, and the ability to read schematics and wiring diagrams
-  Hands-on project experience bringing hardware and software together
-  Operating-system fundamentals

Preferred Qualifications

The qualifications and skills that are important to be successful in this position are as follows:



-  Hands-on experience with CAN, SAE J1939, DBC files, SocketCAN and tools such as CANoe, Kvaser or PCAN
-  Hands-on experience with automotive Ethernet, Ethernet switches and VLANs, NAT/firewall, Wireshark or tcpdump
-  Experience with real-time operating systems and platforms such as QNX or AUTOSAR, and with hypervisors (QNX Hypervisor, Xen or similar)
-  Android or Android Automotive development (Java or Kotlin), ADB/fastboot, Vehicle HAL
-  Embedded Linux and Yocto, bootloaders or device trees
-  Hands-on experience with automotive development platforms, such as those from Qualcomm, NXP or Infineon, or other Arm-based platforms
-  Linux-based telematics (TCU) platforms, connectivity SDKs such as Qualcomm TelSDK, AT commands or GNSS
-  Display, audio or camera integration
-  Truck or automotive electrical systems: 12/24 V power, ignition, harnesses and connectors
-  Working-level understanding of OTA software updates or containers

You do not need to meet every requirement to be a successful candidate. If you have strong fundamentals, enjoy hands-on challenges and learn quickly, we encourage you to apply.

General Description Of All Benefits

As a U.S. PACCAR intern, you have a full range of benefit options including:



-  Competitive salary and 401k with up to a 5% company match
-  Medical, dental, and vision plans for you and your family
-  Paid holidays
-  Flexible spending accounts (FSA) and health savings account (HSA)
-  Life and accidental death and dismemberment insurance
-  EAP services including wellness plans, estate planning, financial counseling and more
-  Global Fortune 500 company with a wide array of growth, training, and development opportunities
-  Work alongside experienced goal-oriented colleagues recognized as experts in their field

Additional Job Board Information

At PACCAR, we value talent and promote growth and development. We carefully consider numerous compensation factors including your education, training, or experience. A reasonable salary range estimate for the Vehicle Software Integration Engineer Intern is $25.00/Hour for students enrolled in an Undergraduate degree program and $30.00/Hour for students enrolled in a Graduate degree program. Additionally, this role is eligible for the full range of benefit options listed above.

PACCAR is an Equal Opportunity Employer/Protected Veteran/Disability corporation. Peterbilt promotes Diversity and Inclusion through mentorship, events, and affinity support groups – The Diversity Council, Peterbilt Women’s Initiative (PBWIN), Veterans Group, Peterbilt Black Organization for Leadership and Development (B.O.L.D) and Peterbilt+ (An LGBTQ support group).
fit_why: Embedded vehicle integration: CAN, RTOS, Linux hardware bring-up, not web

Exowatt is revolutionizing the energy landscape for the AI era with our groundbreaking P3 system that captures solar energy, stores it as heat, and generates electricity on demand. Founded in 2023 and backed by leading investors including Andreessen Horowitz, Sam Altman, and Felicis, we're committed to providing clean, modular, and scalable power that meets the rapidly growing demands of AI infrastructure. Our mission is to make sustainable renewable energy always available and almost free, enabling technological advancement while protecting our planet.

We’re hiring up to six software and AI interns to join our Software team in Austin for Spring 2027. You’ll work in pairs, join a new team each month and build AI tools that help people across Exowatt work faster.

This role is in person at our Austin, TX office.

What You'll Do

Each month, you and your partner join a diﬀerent team, from hardware and manufacturing to finance, HR and go-to-market.

With Each Team, You’ll

Learn how the team works. Sit with the people doing the work and find where AI and better tools can save them time.

Build AI tools. Build agents, automations and internal apps with them, using coding agents like Claude Code, Codex or

Cursor every day.

See it through. Get your work into real use and make sure it works end to end for the people relying on it.

Teach as you go. Help each team learn to use AI in their own work.

What You'll Bring

Currently pursuing a bachelor’s, master’s or PhD in computer science or a related field, graduating in Spring 2027.

Available to work in person in Austin, TX from January 12 to April 16, 2027.

A solid software foundation: you’ve built and shipped your own projects.

You love AI. You already build with AI coding tools and have opinions about which ones work.

A flexible mindset: you’re eager to learn, adapt quickly and enjoy working with people outside engineering.

Clear communication, including with people who aren’t technical.

Nice to Have

None of these are required. If you have a few, tell us about them.

Experience building agents, chatbots or automations that other people use.

Experience with LLM APIs, MCP servers or agent frameworks.

Web development experience, front end or back end.

Hackathons, open source work or a project with real users.

Interest in energy, hardware, manufacturing or how companies run day to day.

Side projects you’re proud of. Send us one link to something you built: a repo, a demo or a write-up.

How We Work

We’re a small team that builds a lot, and our interns ship real work.

You’ll work with people across the company, from the manufacturing floor to finance and HR.

We use AI agents across the company and build much of our own tooling for them.

We build in-house when it beats buying.

Changes are small and ship often.

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.
fit_why: Strong AI-tools/agents/web fit; generalist internal-tools role, in-person Austin

Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube.

Our Summer Internship program is a wonderful opportunity to immerse themselves in an innovative and mission driven culture. Our paid internship program will provide you with hands on mentorship, an opportunity to add real contribution to our company via your internship project, and a possible job offer at the end. You will have the chance to make lifelong friendships, expand your network, and learn all about what it's like to work in a high-growth, fast scaling tech unicorn. You'll take part in company sponsored events and enjoy exploring a new city. Read on below to learn more about this unique internship!

Example Intern Projects



- Applications: Build a new feature or internal tool (web, mobile, or desktop) that streamlines a mission-planning or fleet-management workflow.
- Firmware/Embedded: Develop and debug embedded C/C++ code for a flight controller or sensor module, including bring-up and hardware-in-the-loop testing.
- Machine Learning: Train, evaluate, and integrate a perception or decision-making model (e.g., object detection, sensor fusion) into an autonomy pipeline.
- Systems Development: Extend a platform tool, API, or data pipeline that supports autonomy software, simulation, or cloud infrastructure.

Basic Qualifications



- Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or master's degree in computer science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field
- Proficiency in at least one modern programming language (e.g., C, C++, Python, Java, or JavaScript)
- Solid foundation in data structures, algorithms, and software design principles
- Experience writing, testing, and debugging code, whether through coursework, personal projects, or prior internships

Preferred Qualifications



- Familiarity with version control (e.g., Git) and collaborative development workflows
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to break down ambiguous requirements into working code
- Effective written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively in a team environment
- Exposure to mobile or web application frameworks and full-stack development
- Hands-on experience with embedded systems, microcontrollers, real-time operating systems, or assembly-level debugging
- Coursework or projects involving machine learning, statistics, probability theory, or deep learning frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow)
- Experience with cloud platforms, databases, networking, or distributed systems
- Familiarity with Agile/Scrum development methodologies
- Prior internship, research, or club/competition experience in robotics, autonomy, or aerospace applications
- Interest in or exposure to the defense, aerospace, or autonomous systems industry
fit_why: Example projects lean embedded/firmware, ML perception, and autonomy; mixed with web

JOIN CONTORO ROBOTICS – REVOLUTIONIZING WAREHOUSE AUTOMATION WITH CUTTING-EDGE ROBOTICS

At Contoro Robotics, we're on a mission to solve labor challenges through advanced robotic solutions. Headquartered in Austin, TX, our fast-growing startup is transforming the supply chain industry with our flagship warehouse automation technology. Our team is made up of top-tier experts in robotics, AI, and logistics, working together to push the boundaries of automation.

We’re looking for talented and ambitious individuals to join us on this journey—helping shape the future of robotics while growing alongside a world-class team. If you're passionate about innovation, problem-solving, and making a real-world impact, we want to hear from you!

Contoro · Internship · Austin, TX

About

Contoro Robotics is an Austin based startup focused on warehouse automation. We design a state-of-the-art autonomous truck unloading system capable of lifting boxes over 60 lbs. As an Autonomy Software Intern, you'll join the team that builds the motion planning and autonomous behavior software running on our fleet of unloading robots. You'll help keep that software reliable and easy to build on: you'll investigate issues, discuss improvements, implement well-scope fixes and strengthen the tools and processes the team uses every day. You'll work closely with senior autonomy engineers who will review your code and mentor you. This is a hands-on software role, and the code you write will run on real robots in real customer environments.

In this role, you will:

 - Investigate issues reported from robots in the field and in our test facility, using logs, telemetry, and recorded data to narrow down root causes

 - Implement well-scoped fixes and improvements in Python and C++, and take them through code review to deployment

 - Help improve the reliability, coverage, and organization of the team's automated testing

 - Contribute to the internal developer tools that help engineers understand and debug robot behavior

 - Keep documentation, runbooks, and overall code health up to date as the codebase evolves

 - Work with autonomy, perception, hardware, and test engineers to reproduce problems and verify fixes on real robots

 - Share findings clearly in written updates and team discussions

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Are pursuing a degree in computer science, robotics, mechanical or electrical engineering, or a related field, with a strong software focus

 - Write clean, readable code in Python and/or C++

 - Are comfortable with the Linux command line and Git-based workflows (branches, pull requests, code review)

 - Enjoy debugging: reading unfamiliar code and logs until you understand what is really happening

 - Can clearly communicate what you found, what you changed, and why

 - Have exposure to ROS, motion planning, or robotic systems

 - Have experience writing automated tests or working with CI pipelines and Docker

 - Can work on-site at Contoro's office in Austin, TX for the duration of the internship

 - Are available throughout two continuous terms (e.g., Spring + Summer or Summer + Fall)
fit_why: Robotics autonomy and C++ on real robots, outside his web/AI stack
